plan.analysis: The record 0.941243 has survived ~60 attacks on its own construction: every local, block, subspace, prolongation and smoothing move returns it unchanged, so gains must come from a move that changes the rasterisation/parametrisation rather than the heights. Structurally, R's entire loss is the taper of f*f: the record's g is a tall plateau (||g||inf=0.967 with mass 1) with ~0.3-wide ramps, while T37's edge-singular family reaches only 0.882 because its plateau is wide and low (inf 0.786, 47% of knots at max) — i.e. it needs taller, narrower edge structure. Bets: (1) sub-cell phase shift changes which knots of g carry the max (never tried on the record); (2) forcing p=1/2 at BOTH T37 edges — the analytically flat-onset case its fit never found — plus a tilt can raise that plateau; (3) re-fitting the record's outermost cells to a power-law toe is a 4-parameter non-local move that height-space search cannot see.

experiments.hypothesis: R depends on where the piecewise-linear knots of f*f sit relative to its maximum, not only on the heights. Shifting the whole profile by a fraction of a cell re-rasterises f (each new cell averages two old ones) and produces a genuinely different knot pattern for f*f, i.e. a different local optimum that plain height perturbation cannot reach. F470 showed such shifts give +7e-5 on another basin; they have never been tried on the record.
experiments.change: Base p0555 (N=84992, R=0.941243). For delta in {-0.5,-0.25,+0.25,+0.5}: build h_d by exact cell-averaging of the shifted step function, h_d[i] = (1-u)*h[i+k] + u*h[i+k+1] with k=floor(delta), u=delta-k, index clipped; clip to >=0 and _rescale (h / sqrt(max knot of f*f)). First record R(h_d) before polishing and print it. Then run _lbfgs_log(h_d, 200 iters, 3 s cap, beta=0) followed by _lbfgs_block over _peak_window(frac=0.10, 150 iters, 2 s cap) and one beta=1e4 _lbfgs_log pass (2 s); accept only if R improves. Keep the best over the 4 deltas. Spend all remaining time (until deadline-1 s) on a final full _polish of the best array. Return that array (never a truncated stage).
experiments.prediction: Aim for R>=0.941250 (+7e-6 over the record); stretch 0.94128. The print will show whether any delta beats 0.941243 BEFORE polishing (knot-alignment effect) or only after (basin effect). If all four deltas polish back to 0.941243 exactly, the record is phase-robust and the rasterisation is not the bottleneck.

experiments.hypothesis: T37's fit degenerated to one edge at p=0.5 and the other at p=0.088, giving a wide low plateau (||f*f||inf=0.786, half of f*f knots at max). Analytically, a p=1/2 edge singularity makes f*f exactly constant near that end, so setting BOTH exponents to 0.5 gives flat onsets at both ends; the only cost is the log-divergent cross term in the middle, which a finite spike width w and an asymmetric plateau tilt can absorb. This is the analytically special case the free 9-parameter fit never explored.
experiments.change: Keep the family f(x)=c + tilt*(x-0.5) + 1_{x<wL}*aL*(x+epsL)^(-1/2) + 1_{x>1-wR}*aR*(1-x+epsR)^(-1/2) but FIX pL=pR=0.5 and add tilt (8 free params: c, tilt, log aL, log aR, log wL, log wR, log epsL, log epsR). Rasterise exactly: for cell i use analytic cell averages of (x+eps)^(-1/2), i.e. 2*(sqrt(b+eps)-sqrt(a+eps))/(b-a), no subcell error. Ranges: c in [0.2,5], tilt in [-2,2], aL,aR log-uniform [1e-3,1e2], wL,wR in [1e-3,0.15], epsL,epsR in [1e-6,1e-4]. 3000 random draws at N=1024 scored with exact R, keep top 8, Nelder-Mead (1.5 s each, exact R). Ladder: N=1024 -> 4096 -> 16384 -> 65536, at each level 150-iter _lbfgs_log (exact R, fft) plus one beta=1e4 pass, explicit time checks returning the best COMPLETED level; at the highest completed level re-run Nelder-Mead on the 8 params (1.5 s). Print R, ||f*f||inf and the fraction of f*f knots within 0.1% of max at every level.
experiments.prediction: Aim for R>=0.90 by N=16384 (well above the track's 0.881994) and still rising at 65536; stretch 0.92. The diagnostic is ||f*f||inf with unit mass: T37 sits at 0.786; breaking 0.85 with >50% of knots at max means the p=1/2 tilt family is a genuine second route and the track should continue at higher N. If ||f*f||inf stays ~0.78 and R plateaus at 0.88-0.89 regardless of N, two-sided sqrt singularities cannot reach the record's tall plateau.

experiments.hypothesis: The record's f*f ramp is limited by the finite values of its outermost cells: a two-sided power-law toe (the capped-edge-singularity family of F474/F450) rises steeply to the first substantial cell and thereby steepens the f*f ramp, while costing almost no mass and hence only a small middle bump. Unlike F468/F473, which copied or mirrored the existing toe, this REPLACES the outer cells by a smooth 4-parameter law, a low-dimensional non-local move that the saturated exact-R gradient cannot generate.
experiments.change: Base p0555 (N=84992). Let x=(arange(N)+0.5)/N. For K in {256, 1024, 4096}: for the first K and last K cells, replace h by A*(x+1e-4)^(-p) and A'*(1-x+1e-4)^(-p') respectively, leaving the interior untouched, then _rescale. Optimise the 4 parameters (log A_L, p_L in [0,0.95], log A_R, p_R) with Nelder-Mead against exact R at full N (each eval ~2 fftconvolve, ~2 ms; cap 2.5 s per K, 250 iters max); initialise at A=0.3*h_edge-ish and p=0.5. Accept the K whose optimised toe has highest R only if it beats 0.941243. Then _rescale and run _lbfgs_log(200 iters, 4 s, beta=0) plus _lbfgs_block over _peak_window(frac=0.08, 120 iters, 3 s) and one beta=1e3 pass; keep any improvement. Finish with a full _polish of the best array using all remaining time to deadline-1 s.

plan.analysis: The record 0.941243 is stable under every local, prolongation, subspace, phase-shift, toe-replacement and block-additive move tried (F288, F461, F472, F478, F484-F486); so the defect is not obvious low-amplitude mass. What the diagnostics do show on p0555 is a soft top: 18.24% of f*f knots within 0.1% of max but 42.77% within 5% — a broad, slightly curved shoulder. The exact-max gradient touches only the argmax, and logsumexp up to beta=1e8 collapses onto it too, so no gradient has ever asked the top 40% of knots to be made equal. I bet the main line can be moved by a *windowed-max* (moving-average) surrogate whose gradient is spread over W knots of the top, i.e. a surrogate whose optimum is a flat top. For the two side tracks: T38's toe-replacement premise is refuted twice, so its follow-up should instead give the toe *sub-cell degrees of freedom* (local 4x refinement, then toe-only exact-R optimization); T37's 8-parameter sqrt-singular family is at 0.881998 with 46.8% of knots exactly at max, so the follow-up is a free-form polish to test whether the family's shape is the ceiling.

experiments.hypothesis: The record's top is slightly curved (only 18.24% of knots within 0.1% of max, 42.77% within 5%). Minimising a windowed-max surrogate log(mean of L over a window of 2W+1 knots) gives a gradient spread over the *whole* top ~2W knots, pushing them down relative to the shoulders and flattening the top — a coherent move the exact-max/logsumexp gradients cannot make because they concentrate on one knot.
experiments.change: Base p0555, reuse all helpers. Add _fun_grad_win(h, W): compute Lf=_knots(h), num,dq; moving average M = cumsum-based mean of Lf over window [k-W,k+W] (clip at ends, divide by actual count); k*=argmax(M), Mval=M[k*]; gLf = -dq/num; gLf[k*-W:k*+W+1] += 1.0/(Mval*count); grad = _backprop(gLf,h) + 2/s; val = -log(num)+2log(s)+log(Mval). Then: for W in (16,64,256,1024,4096): run _lbfgs_log(h, fg=lambda hh: _fun_grad_win(hh,W), maxiter=150, time cap min(deadline-2, now+4)); print exact R before/after; run _short_polish (sharp) and accept only if exact R > best+1e-12. Then repeat the ladder once more with window half-width scaled 0.5 and center offset by a random ±W/2 (use a centre-shifted window variant) while time remains, then one final _polish and return best. Never return worse than the base.
experiments.prediction: Aim R>=0.941248 (+5e-6), stretch 0.94130. If every W's polished R snaps back to exactly 0.941243, the top curvature is not the loss and the main line must go non-smooth/resolutional; if some W survives sharp polish with a gain, the windowed-max surrogate is a new working move.

experiments.hypothesis: T38's premise (the toe's finite values limit the f*f ramp) was already refuted by replacing values with power laws; what was never tested is whether the toe is limited by its *discretisation*. Refining only the outer cells into 4 sub-cells per cell leaves f and R exactly unchanged but gives the optimizer sub-cell freedom precisely where the edge ramp is formed, so a toe-only exact-R optimization can move the ramp in a way global prolongation (F478, which polishes all cells) cannot.
experiments.change: Base p0566 (N=84992). Build a refined array h2 of length N+6K for K=512 (and, if time, K=64 and K=2048): first K cells each replaced by 4 equal sub-cells of the same height (widths 1/4, mass preserved), last K likewise, middle untouched. R(h2) must equal R(h) to 1e-12 (print this check). Then run _lbfgs_block(h2, free=all indices of the two refined toe regions (8K cells), maxiter=150, time cap 8 s, beta=0) then beta=1e3 and 1e4 passes (60 iters each), then _short_polish, comparing exact R to the base's 0.941243. Accept and print dR per K; try the next K only if time remains after the first. Also print the new toe cells' mean/partition to show in what direction the optimizer moved them.
experiments.prediction: Aim +1e-6 or more on the track (>=0.941244); a gain means the edge ramp is discretisation-limited and local refinement is the right lever. If R stays at 0.941243 for K=512 within a few 1e-9, the toe's values are not the constraint even with sub-cell freedom, and T38 should be closed in favour of the shoulder/windowed-max direction.

experiments.hypothesis: p0563 is the optimum of an 8-parameter family (c, tilt, two sqrt spikes, widths, eps) yet it has 0% zeros and 46.8% of f*f knots exactly at max; the family may simply be unable to express the best shape of its class. plan.analysis: The record 0.941243 has absorbed ~70 local and semi-global moves; every gradient, toe, staircase-splitting and multiresolution recipe on it returns exactly the same R. So slot 1 needs a move that is non-local in a way gradients cannot produce: a monotone *warp of the x-axis* (mass-preserving, with Jacobian), which reshapes the whole profile at once and is exactly R-invariant only for linear warps — an untried class. Slots 2 and 3 go elsewhere: p0447 (0.940995) is a genuinely different geometry never pushed, and nothing in this run has been seeded from the one measured analytic fact we have — for f ~ x^-1/2 truncated at 1, f*f is *exactly constant* on [0,1] (no end ramp at all), giving R≈0.899 in closed form, well above what the capped power-law families (T34/T37, 0.882) ever reached because their fits degenerated (F480/F487). That is the most promising fresh start.

experiments.hypothesis: Every move tried on the record changes heights cell-by-cell; none has changed the *positions* of the mass along the axis. A smooth monotone warp x->phi(x) applied to the step function (with the Jacobian factor, so mass is conserved) is a low-dimensional global reshaping: if the record's remaining loss is in the width/placement of the f*f ramps rather than in the local heights, a warp will raise exact R immediately, before any polish.
experiments.change: Base p0573 (N=84992). h=clip(start). Let u=(arange(N)+0.5)/N. Define phi(u)=u+sum_{k=1..K} a_k*sin(pi*k*u) with K=5 (vanishing at 0 and 1 so support is preserved) and phi'=1+sum a_k*pi*k*cos(pi*k*u). Define h_warp(a) = np.interp(phi(u), u, h) * phi'(u) / mean(phi')  (clipped at 0). Write R_warp(a)=R_of(h_warp(a)). First do a coarse coordinate scan: for each k, try a_k in {-0.02,-0.01,0,0.01,0.02} and keep the best (this is ~25 evals, ~0.1 s). Then run scipy Nelder-Mead on a with |a_k|<=0.06, maxiter 400, capped at 15 s, objective = -R_warp. Print R_warp at the identity (must equal the start R to 1e-12 — verify the Jacobian code), the best R_warp and the a vector. Accept only if R_warp > R(start); then run _rescale and the full _polish with all remaining time (deadline-0.5 s). If the coarse scan and Nelder-Mead both return the identity, additionally try a piecewise warp: phi with a single narrow bump of width 0.05N centred at the f*f argmax knot (index from np.argmax(_knots(h))) and one at each toe, amplitude scanned over +-0.02..0.08, then polish.
experiments.prediction: Aim R>=0.94125 (+6e-6); a win shows as R_warp > 0.941243 *before* polish, i.e. the record's mass placement is off, not just its heights. If R_warp never exceeds the start by more than 1e-9 for any warp, the record is stationary under mass-placement too, and the remaining 5.9% is not reachable from this basin.

experiments.hypothesis: p0447 (0.940995) is a different-geometry construction that has never been taken to high resolution. All of its cells are at the same grid, so the shape is fully described at its native N; splitting each cell into two *unequal* halves (random 55/45..70/30 split, mass-preserving) gives real sub-cell degrees of freedom that a plain staircase doubling (F288) does not, and from a non-saturated construction those extra degrees of freedom are not pinned.
experiments.change: Base p0447. Let rng=np.random.default_rng(7). Build h2 of length 2N: for each cell i, split into two cells with fractions w and 1-w where w = 0.5 + rng.uniform(-0.18,0.18) (heights h_i*2w, h_i*2(1-w) so the mass of each pair is preserved). Check R_of(h2) within 1e-10 of R_of(base); print it. Then run the full pipeline on h2 with all available time: _lbfgs_log(h2, 250, beta=0) -> beta in {1e2,1e3,1e4} -> _lbfgs_block over _peak_window(frac=0.06,0.12,0.25) -> a final _polish; after each accepted improvement, print exact R and N. If a plateau is hit with >15 s left, do one more randomized split of the current best (same recipe) up to N<=250000 and repeat the polish, keeping only exact-R improvements. Return the best array seen (never below the start).
experiments.prediction: Aim >=0.94105 on this track (+5e-5 over p0447) and above 0.941243 if the sub-cell freedom is real; the diagnostic is the R after the *unequal* split plus one L-BFGS pass — if it rises by >1e-6, the geometry is resolution-limited and further splits should be laddered.

experiments.hypothesis: Closed form: for f(x)=A*x^{-1/2} on [0,1], (f*f)(x)=pi*A^2 exactly for all x in [0,1], so f*f has NO left ramp at all (R~0.899 by direct quadrature of the right ramp 2*arcsin((2-x)/x)). The capped/spike families of T34/T37 never expressed this because their fits collapsed (F480/F487). Seeding exactly at the singular-plus-plateau profile therefore lands in a genuinely different, much flatter-plateau basin than anything currently on the map.
experiments.change: From scratch (ignore start). Family: f(x) = A*(x+epsL)^{-pL} + B + C*(1-x+epsR)^{-pR} on [0,1] with parameters log A, pL in [0.30,0.60], B, log C, pR in [0.0,0.45], epsL,epsR in [1e-6,1e-2]. Rasterise at N=2048 by 16-subcell averaging per cell (analytic integral of x^{-p} = ((b)^{1-p}-(a)^{1-p})/(1-p)), so the singularity is integrated exactly. Initialise at pL=pR=0.5, B=0, A=C, eps=1e-4. Optimise the 7 params against exact R_of: coarse random search (3000 samples log-uniform, capped 3 s), then Nelder-Mead 600 iters capped 6 s, printing R at every accepted best. Then escalate: mass-preserving 2x prolongation to 4096, 8192, 16384, 32768, at each level free-form _lbfgs_log (200 iters, beta=0) + one _lbfgs_block on _peak_window(0.10); print exact R per level. Spend all remaining time in the beta ladder (1e2,1e3,1e4,1e5) plus sharp polish on the best level, accepting only exact-R gains.
experiments.prediction: Aim R>=0.905 at N=2048 (verifying the closed-form ~0.899 prediction with the free B and pR) and >=0.93 after the ladder; a stretch of 0.94+. experiments.hypothesis: Closed form: for f(x)=A*x^{-1/2} on [0,1], (f*f)(x)=pi*A^2 exactly for all x in [0,1], so f*f has NO left ramp at all (R~0.899 by direct quadrature of the right ramp 2*arcsin((2-x)/x)). The capped/spike families of T34/T37 never expressed this because their fits collapsed (F480/F487). Seeding exactly at the singular-plus-plateau profile therefore lands in a genuinely different, much flatter-plateau basin than anything currently on the map.
experiments.change: From scratch (ignore start). plan.analysis: The record 0.941243 is a saturated local optimum: ~100 experiments on that exact construction (toes, warps, sub-cells, coarsening, block-additive, subspace, prolongation) all return the start unchanged, and the max knot is degenerate (argmax jumps between 0.338/0.666/0.813 across reports), so the exact-max gradient keeps re-sharpening a single knot instead of levelling the plateau. Reading the numbers as a trapezoid: ||g||inf=0.9674, ||g||2^2=0.9105, effective width 1/0.9674=1.034, plateau 0.852 with 0.182 of ramp. So the remaining loss is entirely ramp/tilt and top unevenness. I bet on (1) a clipped-energy surrogate that explicitly flattens the top instead of sharpening it, (2) a cheap global envelope/tilt probe on p0447's distinct geometry (T39), and (3) a strictly time-boxed restart of T40's closed-form singular family, which reached 0.882 at N=2048 before being killed by the CPU limit.

experiments.hypothesis: The exact-R gradient (-dq/num + 1/Lmax at one knot) can only raise the single argmax knot, and the record's max is degenerate, so every local pass sharpens a peak that should be levelled. Replacing ||g||inf by a fixed cap c=alpha*max(g) turns the problem into 'maximise mass under the cap', whose gradient pushes the whole plateau up to c and ignores knots already above it — a direction the ratio gradient cannot produce. Exact-R polish afterwards recovers the ratio.
experiments.change: Base p0573 (N=84992). Keep all its helpers. Add _fun_grad_clip(h, alpha): compute num, dq-style weights, Lf = _knots(h) as in _num_and_dq; M = Lf.max(); c = alpha*M; u = np.where(Lf < c, Lf, 0.0); E = sum over knots of (u_j^2+u_j u_{j+1}+u_{j+1}^2)/3 using the same triangular formula on u; dE/dLf = the same (2a+b, a+2b)/3 assembly applied to u, multiplied by (Lf < c); s = h.sum(); grad = _backprop(dE/E, h) - 2.0/s; value = -log(E) + 2*log(s) (scale invariant). Then, budgeted by time.process_time(): for alpha in (0.999, 0.99, 0.97): run _lbfgs_log with fg=lambda hh: _fun_grad_clip(hh, alpha) for 60 iters or 3 s, then 2 s of exact-R _lbfgs_log(beta=0), keeping the best by exact R_of. After the alpha sweep, spend ALL remaining time to deadline-0.8 s in the existing alternation: exact _lbfgs_log(200 iters, 4 s) -> beta 1e3,1e4 passes -> _lbfgs_block over _peak_window(0.08) -> repeat, always keeping the best exact-R array and returning it. info.open_why: Need p0447's geometry for the T39 follow-up, p0566/T38's toe-refinement context and F485/F491/F496 to see what structural moves on the record have already failed, and F474 for the singular-family idea behind T40.

plan.analysis: The record 0.941243 is a fixed point for every height-space move we have (gradients, capped/windowed/p-norm surrogates, warps, upsampling at 2x/3x/4x, toe refinement, multigrid, block-additive): ~200 attempts, all zero. Its f*f is a trapezoid with ~0.09-wide ramps; since R=1 is attained by any f with f*f an exact rectangle, the only route up is to shorten those ramps, i.e. move mass between peak and shoulders. Ramp shortening is exactly what a singular edge gives (f~x^-1/2 makes f*f jump), and T40's diagnostic now says the additive two-sided singular family degenerates (one side at p=0.088, max at 0.500) and caps near 0.882 — the missing ingredient is a free plateau length. So: one main slot on global contrast reshaping of the record (the Euler-Lagrange direction), one T40 follow-up with a jump-plateau-jump family that can put a true jump at each end of f*f, one revive of rank-pruning+pedestal on the record.

experiments.hypothesis: R=1 iff f*f is an exact rectangle, so the deficit lives entirely in f*f's two ramps. The record sits at one fixed contrast (max/mean 147) which sets how much mass is in the shoulders vs the peak; a monotone power reshaping h^gamma (mass-preserving, then rescaled) moves mass between peak and shoulders while staying inside the family that contains the record at gamma=1, and the exact-R polish from a different gamma can land in a different local optimum. Nothing on this line has ever changed the global peak-to-shoulder contrast of the record before polishing.
experiments.change: Base p0573 (N=84992). Keep all its helpers (_knots, R_of, _fun_grad, _lbfgs_log, _lbfgs_block, _peak_window, _rescale). Loop over gamma in [0.60, 0.75, 0.85, 1.15, 1.30, 1.50]: h_g = _rescale(h**gamma / h**gamma.mean()) (monotone, keeps shape at gamma=1 exactly). For each, print R immediately after reshaping, then spend a fixed 6 s slice: _lbfgs_log(h_g, 250, slice_deadline, beta=0), then one beta=1e3 pass (100 iters, 3 s), then _lbfgs_block on _peak_window(0.10) (100 iters, 3 s). Keep the best exact-R array over all gammas and over the unmodified record. After the gamma scan, spend ALL remaining time to deadline-0.5 s alternating _lbfgs_log(beta=0, 400 iters, ~8 s) and _peak_window(0.05/0.15) block passes on the incumbent, keeping the best exact R each time. Return the best array. Guard every stage with time.process_time() and a hard deadline of t0 + 0.88*budget.
experiments.prediction: Aim R >= 0.94126 (+1.7e-5) with the winning gamma printed. Diagnostic: if every gamma's post-reshape R is below 0.941243 and all polishes snap back to exactly 0.941243, contrast is not the limiting factor and the record's basin is isolated under monotone reshaping — then the whole line must be abandoned for a new geometry. If a gamma!=1 keeps a post-polish gain, record which direction (gamma<1 or >1) and the next generation scans that side finely.

experiments.hypothesis: T40's diagnostic fired: the additive two-sided family degenerated (pL=0.088 one side, max of f*f at 0.500, 24.9% of knots at max — i.e. it settles for a wide low plateau, not a jump). The analytic fact F501 gives is that a single x^-1/2 edge makes f*f jump at that end with NO ramp; T40's family could never exploit it because it had no plateau-length parameter and bounded p away from the useful geometry. A family with a free plateau interval and an independent sqrt edge on each side can put a genuine jump at BOTH ends of f*f, which is exactly the degree of freedom the record lacks.
experiments.change: From p0583 (ignore start contents). New family on [0,1]: f(x) = a*(x+epsL)^(-1/2) for x < t0; c for t0 <= x <= t1; b*(1-x+epsR)^(-1/2) for x > t1. 7 parameters: (log a, log b, log c, t0 in [0.02,0.95], t1 in [t0+0.03, 0.98], log epsL, log epsR in [1e-4, 3e-2]); exponent fixed at 1/2. Rasterise at N with 8-subcell averaging of this exact function (use 16 subcells for the first/last 2 cells where the singularity lives), clip at 0, nonneg. Stage A (<=2 s): 1500 seeded random draws (log-uniform a,b,c; t0,t1 sorted), exact R, keep top 6. Stage B (<=9 s): Nelder-Mead on the 7 params at N=1024 from each of the top 6, maxiter 250 each, time-boxed. Stage C (<=6 s): re-run Nelder-Mead from the incumbent at N=2048 then N=4096. Stage D (<=10 s): at N=8192, _lbfgs_log on the rasterised heights at N=8192 (free log-heights, exact R, 150 iters) then one beta=1e3 pass then _peak_window(0.08) block pass (this is only a mild polish of the family solution — do NOT let it wander far: cap stages at 150 iters). Stage E: all remaining time to deadline-0.85*budget alternating _lbfgs_log (beta=0 and 1e3) and peak-window block polish at N=8192, keeping the best exact-R array. Print R after each stage plus the 7 fitted parameters at N=4096 and the fractions of f*f knots within 0.1%/5% of max. Return the best array.
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.90 at N=8192 (a jump over the track's 0.881998); stretch 0.941243+. Diagnostic: the printed near-max fractions decide it — if the fitted t1-t0 is pinned at its upper bound and 40%+ of f*f knots are within 0.1% of max, the jump-plateau-jump family is real and one more escalation at N=32768/65536 is the next step; if t1-t0 collapses to ~0 and 25% of knots sit at max again, the family is capped at 0.89 and T40 closes.

experiments.hypothesis: F385 (rank-based pruning + pedestal redistribution) worked on a 47.7%-zero basin and was never tried on the record. It is the one large, non-local mass move in the book: deleting the smallest-height cells and re-injecting their mass as a pedestal raises f*f's low tails while lowering the plateau — precisely the direction the Euler-Lagrange argument for 'g as rectangular as possible' prescribes. Every move tried on the record so far was local in height magnitude (multiplying/smoothing/shifting); this one sets a chunk of cells to exactly zero and puts the mass elsewhere in one step.
experiments.change: Base p0573 (N=84992). Keep _rescale, R_of, _lbfgs_log, _lbfgs_block, _peak_window. For q in (0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.25) and for pedestal mode in 3 variants: (i) uniform over all N cells, (ii) uniform over the middle 50% of the support, (iii) added proportional to h among the top 20% of cells. plan.analysis: The record 0.941243 is a saturated local max: ~126 failed moves on that exact construction — cell-wise gradients, toe/power-law replacement, rank pruning+pedestal, axis warp, gamma re-shaping, upsampling ladders, coarse-to-fine rebuilds. What has NOT been tried is (a) smoothing the whole objective before the max (blurring f*f), which changes the landscape at scale w and lets mass move in coordinated directions where the sharp gradient is exactly zero, (b) rank-preserving monotone rearrangement (T41's non-local mass move, but as a permutation rather than pruning), and (c) applying the strongest modern recipe (beta->1e7 continuation) to L1's untouched 0.940795 basin. I bet on these three: blurred-objective homotopy (main), rearrangement (T41), and an F442/F448 revival on p0491.

experiments.hypothesis: All sharp-objective moves fail because the record is a true local max, so any first-order descent is impossible. Blurring f*f with a normalized Gaussian of width w (a graduated-smoothing homotopy, distinct from the beta-softmax which only softens the max) creates a landscape whose maximizer differs at scale w; annealing w from ~64 cells to 0 walks the construction through coordinated mass moves that the sharp gradient cannot see, and should land in a neighbouring basin with higher R.
experiments.change: Base p0573 (N=84992). Keep all helpers. Add _fun_grad_blur(h, w): compute Lf=_knots(h); build kernel k = normalized Gaussian with sigma=w, radius ceil(3w)+1; Gb = np.convolve(Lf, k, mode='same') (zero-extended ends); num=sum(a*a+a*b+b*b)/3 on a=Gb[:-1],b=Gb[1:]; dq as in _num_and_dq; S=sum((a+b)/2) (trapezoid mass of Gb); M=Gb.max(), m=argmax; gGb = -dq/num + (0.5 at both ends incl. -0.5 shift)/S + e_m/M; then gG = np.convolve(gGb, k, mode='same') (self-adjoint); grad = _backprop(gG, h) + 2/sum(h); val = -log(num)+log(S)+log(M). Write _lbfgs_log_blur(h0, w, iters, deadline) mirroring _lbfgs_log but with that gradient (log-parametrisation on active cells, L-BFGS-B, same bounds/callback). Ladder: for w in (64, 32, 16, 8, 4, 2): run 120 iters (time-capped, ~3 s each), _rescale, compute exact R_of, keep best; after each w also do one 60-iter w=0 sharp pass (_lbfgs_log). Then one beta=1e3 pass (80 iters) and _lbfgs_block on _peak_window(frac=0.08, 120 iters). Finish by spending ALL remaining time alternating _polish(best,...) and _short_polish(best,...) until deadline-0.5 s, always returning the best exact-R array seen. Print exact R at every stage and the per-w table.

experiments.hypothesis: T41's premise (large non-local mass moves are the only untried class on the record) is right, but rank-based PRUNING+pedestal failed because it destroyed mass. The same rank information used as a rank-preserving monotone REARRANGEMENT — placing the existing height multiset in a V-shape (largest at the two edges, smallest at the centre, exactly the structure the steep-ramp theory wants) — is a genuinely non-local move that costs no mass at all, and a blend path from the record makes it a continuous family.

plan.analysis: The record p0573 is saturated: 20+ generations of per-cell, multiplicative, rank, blur and toe moves all return it unchanged, and its deficit matches a trapezoid with 0.30-wide ramps — a shape-level limit, not a gradient one. experiments.hypothesis: p0594 (0.935035, N=254974) has ||f*f||_2^2 = 0.914968 (higher than the record's 0.910514) but ||f*f||_inf = 0.978540 (vs 0.967353), with its max at 0.300 of support and only 11.34% of knots within 0.1% of max. experiments.change: Base p0594, keep every helper (R_of, _knots, _num_and_dq, _backprop, _rescale, _lbfgs_log, _lbfgs_block, _peak_window, _polish). experiments.hypothesis: Every construction on the board is a fixed-grid height vector (or a fixed analytic edge-singular law, capped near 0.882). A variable-width contiguous block family — K blocks on [0,1] with free boundaries and free heights, rasterised exactly by overlap — has a very different landscape: block boundaries let the support's plateau/ramp structure move by whole-cell jumps that per-cell gradients cannot produce, and the coarse-to-fine re-fit at fixed boundary parameters escapes the discretisation traps that killed F293's random multiset starts.

slots.text: Slot 1 (main): build on the strongest line, as you judge best (any program can be the base).

Slot 2 (explore: continue side track T42): it was opened at generation 237 (a backtrack to p0491) and is owed a follow-up, even if it started below its base. Its programs so far:
- p0597 (gen 237, deep, from p0491): 0.940795, +0.000000 on its start: p0491 is a distinct, much less explored basin (N=42496, 20.9% zeros, max/mean 97, f*f argmax 0.551, 19.6% of …
The base must be one of its programs (normally its best, p0597). It is judged against the track's own best (0.940795).

Slot 3 (explore: bold): a genuinely different kind of construction or search, not a refinement of the current best. Any base, including p0001 (Code Zero, the trivial starting program, to build from nothing) (Code Zero, to build from nothing).

info.open_why: The bold slot needs a genuinely different construction: T40's edge-singular family (p0583/F450/F474) is the only non-refinement route that ever produced a high score, and F507/F501 will show what its best variant was and why it stalled, while p0566 shows the current best toe-refinement state to judg

plan.analysis: The record 0.941243 has absorbed ~20 generations of failed moves (blur, clip-plateau, rearrangement, prune+pedestal, upsample-repolish, toe families): it is a saturated local optimum whose deficit is structural (plateau+ramps), so the main slot should test the one cheap move class never tried on it — breaking the lattice by fractional-phase resampling at fixed N. The only basin with a higher ||f*f||_2^2 than the record (p0594, 0.914968 vs 0.910514) is still 0.006 short and already resisted top-m flattening, so it is not a next-generation bet. Exploration slots: T43's block family never produced a valid program (an off-by-one in the boundary array), so it must be repaired and given a full grid-phase continuation; T21's only proven lever is sparsity plus progressive halve-and-refine (F465), untried on p0600.

experiments.hypothesis: The record's f*f knots sit on a fixed lattice (it is an exact staircase doubling), and every failed move changed heights only. A mass-preserving fractional-phase resample at fixed N changes which knot positions f*f has, giving L-BFGS a different discrete landscape in which the saturated plateau/ramp compromise may be re-negotiated; F470 (+7e-5 on a 0.908 basin) shows phase shifts can pay.
experiments.change: Base p0573, keep every helper. Add _resample_shift(h, delta): F=np.concatenate(([0.0],np.cumsum(h))); y=np.interp(np.arange(h.size+1)+delta, np.arange(h.size+1), F); h2=np.diff(y) (exact piecewise-constant cell integrals of the shifted profile, mass-preserving up to the truncated ends). Sweep delta in (0.15,0.30,0.50,0.70,0.85) and delta=0.0: h=_rescale(_resample_shift(base,delta)), run _short_polish with a 3.5 s cap, print 'delta=%.2f R=%.12f N=%d'. Keep the best delta by exact R_of. Then spend the remaining time on that best candidate: (a) exact 2x non-staircase resample (_resample_shift(h,0.5) on a 2n grid via splitting each cell into two half-cells, i.e. h2=np.repeat(h,2) then _resample_shift(h2,0.5)), _rescale, then _lbfgs_log 120 it beta=0, then beta=1e3 and 1e5 (80 it each), (b) _lbfgs_block on _peak_window(frac=0.05) and frac=0.15 (100 it each). Accept a candidate only if exact R_of strictly exceeds the incumbent; loop (a)+(b) until the deadline is within 0.7 s. Print final R, N, zero fraction, and ||f*f||_inf and ||f*f||_2^2 with unit-mass scaling.
experiments.prediction: Aim R >= 0.941250 (>+7e-6, a real record gain), stretch 0.94130. Diagnostic: print argmax and the 0.1%-near-max knot fraction for every delta. If all deltas and the 0.5-shifted 2x resample return exactly 0.9412430 after full polish, the record is invariant under lattice phase and its deficit is purely structural — that redirects all future main-line effort away from the record and into p0594-style basins.

experiments.hypothesis: T43 died on an indexing bug, not on its premise: a K-block contiguous family with free boundaries plus a full grid-phase continuation is genuinely untried and, unlike the analytic edge-singular families (capped at ~0.882), it can represent the record's broad off-centre plateau. Its value is either a competitive score from scratch or a qualitatively different basin (symmetric, ~50% of knots near max) to seed later tracks.
experiments.change: From Code Zero (use start only as fallback seed). Parametrise K=6 contiguous blocks on [0,1]: gaps = exp(g)/sum(exp(g)) with g of length 5, boundaries b = np.concatenate(([0.0], np.cumsum(gaps))) so len(b)==K+1 (assert this; the previous crash was b of size 6 used at b[k+1] for k up to 5); heights = exp(a) with a of length 5 and a_0 fixed to 0 (scale invariance). Rasterise exactly at N=4096: for each cell i, h[i] = (1/N)*sum_k height_k*overlap([i/N,(i+1)/N],[b_k,b_{k+1}]) computed with np.minimum/np.maximum clips over the K blocks (no index k+1 beyond K-1). Objective = exact R_of on the rasterised array. Stage 1: 30 random starts (log-uniform gaps in [1e-2,1], log-uniform heights in [1e-2,1e2]), Nelder-Mead on the 11 parameters, each capped at 0.6 s of CPU with a time guard; keep the best 3 and re-run Nelder-Mead on them. Stage 2: take the best rasterisation and stop using the block model — run _lbfgs_log at N=4096 with beta=0 then 1e2 then 1e3 (100 it each), then _lbfgs_block on _peak_window(frac=0.10). Stage 3: exact 2x staircase prolongation (np.repeat/2**0.5) to 8192 then 16384 with the same beta ladder plus peak-window block polish, accepting only exact-R gains, until the deadline is within 0.7 s. Wrap every stage in try/except with fallback to the current best valid array; check at exit that the result is finite, non-negative, sum>0, size<=1e6.
experiments.prediction: Aim R >= 0.92 at N=16384 (clear win over the edge-singular bootstraps' 0.882), stretch 0.94. Diagnostic to print: the fitted block boundaries and heights and the location of argmax(f*f). If argmax lands near 0.5 with more than 40% of knots within 1% of max, T43 has produced a basin qualitatively different from the record's (argmax 0.666, 34.5%) and it becomes a long-lived side track even at 0.92.

experiments.hypothesis: p0600 (0.940460, N=169984, 24.9% zeros) only ever gained from sparsity plus grid changes. F465 showed a progressive halve-and-refine path (coarsen with mass preservation, re-polish sharply, prolongate back) finds a different local optimum on exactly this kind of fine, staircase-saturated construction, and it has never been applied on T21.
experiments.change: Base p0600 (N=169984), keep every helper. Stage A: build coarse copies by mass-preserving averaging h_c[i] = mean(h[i*k:(i+1)*k]) for k=2 (N=84992) and k=4 (N=42496), _rescale each; for each coarse copy run _lbfgs_log(beta=0, 150 it, 3 s cap) then _lbfgs_block on _peak_window(frac=0.08) (80 it, 2 s cap), then one rank-prune cycle (zero the q=0.10 smallest positive cells, restore 1e-3*local mean into the longest zero run, _rescale, sharp _lbfgs_log 80 it), printing 'coarse k=%d R=%.9f zero=%.3f' after each; keep the best coarse array by exact R_of. Stage B: prolongate the best coarse result back to the base N with exact 2x/4x staircase repeat (_rescale(h)/sqrt(k)), then run, alternating to the deadline minus 0.7 s: p-norm ladder p=4,8,16,32 (80 it each) and beta ladder 1e2,1e3,1e5 (60 it each), interleaved with _lbfgs_block peak-window polishes at frac 0.05 and 0.15; accept a stage only if exact R_of strictly improves on the incumbent, and keep the overall best against the base 0.940460. Print final R, N, zero fraction, max/mean, near-max fraction.

plan.analysis: The record is a saturated cell-local optimum: 18 generations and >100 moves on it have returned it unchanged, and the just-completed F529 result shows the only recent real gains come from changing the coordinate system / resolution path, not from polishing heights. I bet main-slot value is in a different objective (smoothed-target least squares, which moves mass into f*f valleys nonlocally) rather than another beta/p-norm sweep. T43's collapse to max/mean 1.09 is a seeding/objective bug (smoothness penalty plus numeric gradient), so its block idea deserves one repaired test with exact analytic gradients from spiky seeds. For the revive, F450's edge-singular family is the one class that directly attacks the ramp width, and it has never been applied as a local replacement of the record's outer cells.

plan.analysis: The record line (p0616, 0.941243) has produced nothing in 19 generations: every cell-level, window-level, parametric-toe and soft-max move has failed on that exact construction. Two facts are still unexploited on it: F353/F288 say the 84992 heights are an *exact staircase doubling* of a 42496 array, so the coarse array's R is identical and the coarse problem is half-size and smoother — a coarsen-polish-prolongate cycle has never been run on the record (F523 was upsampling, F526 a phase resample). Meanwhile T21 (p0608, 0.940644) is the only live gaining line, via F529's halve-and-refine; its natural extension is a full 3-level V-cycle with pruning. T44's parametric toe replacement failed (F533), so I bet the toe instead needs *extra discretisation*, not a prescribed shape.

experiments.hypothesis: The record is an exact 2x staircase, so halving it by pairwise mean gives an array h_c with R(h_c) = R(record) exactly, on a half-size problem whose gradients are averaged (less saturated) and therefore less stuck. Any gain found at 42496 transfers verbatim to 84992 by repeat(h_c,2) — a free improvement with no fine-grid search. Additionally a smoothed prolongation breaks the staircase symmetry so the fine re-polish can land in a different fine basin.
experiments.change: Use start=p0616, keep all existing helpers. Step 0 (diagnostic): h_c = 0.5*(h[0::2]+h[1::2]), rescale, print 'staircase err=%.2e Rcoarse=%.12f Rfine=%.12f' with err = max|h - repeat(h_c,2)|/(max h), and both R values. Step 1 (coarse search, ~55% of budget, deadline_c = t0+0.55*budget): at N=42496 run in order, each accepted only if exact R_of strictly improves: _lbfgs_log(h_c, 400 it, beta=0); beta ladder 1e3, 1e4, 1e5 (150 it each); p-norm ladder p=4,8,16 (100 it each); _lbfgs_block on _peak_window(frac=0.05) and frac=0.15 (150 it each); one rank-prune cycle (zero q=0.10 smallest positive cells, restore 1e-3*local mean into the longest zero run, rescale, _lbfgs_log 100 it). Print R after every stage as 'coarse %s R=%.9f dR=%+.2e'. Step 2 (prolongate): build fine A = _rescale(np.repeat(h_c_best,2)); fine B = _rescale(np.repeat(_gauss_smooth(h_c_best, sigma=1.5),2)) where _gauss_smooth is a normalized 7-tap Gaussian over the coarse index. Report R(A), R(B). Step 3: alternate until deadline-0.7 s: _lbfgs_log(beta=0, 300 it) then _lbfgs_log(beta=1e5, 120 it) then _lbfgs_block(peak frac 0.05, 100 it) on the incumbent, starting from whichever of A,B has higher R and re-starting from the other one after the first stalls; accept only exact R improvements. Return the best array seen, compared against the untouched base.
experiments.prediction: Aim R >= 0.941250, stretch 0.941270. Diagnostics: staircase err should be ~0 and Rcoarse == Rfine to <1e-9 (confirming F353); if the coarse polish then raises coarse R by >1e-6 the fine grid is not load-bearing and the win is immediate; if coarse R stalls at the same value and only the smoothed prolongation changes anything, that says the record's plateau is a coarse-grid local optimum, which is a strong fact for planning the next main slot.

experiments.hypothesis: F533 showed that prescribing an analytic x^-p sub-cell shape for the toe cells cannot improve the record. The complementary possibility is that the toe is limited by *discretisation*, not by shape: doubling the grid (an exact staircase that leaves R bit-identical) and freeing only the first 2J half-cells gives the toe genuine sub-cell freedom with no parametric assumption. If the f*f ramp/tail is limited by the finite toe cells, this must show a positive dR at 2x that the parametric family could not reach.
experiments.change: Use start=p0616. (a) Build h2 = _rescale(np.repeat(h,2)) at N=169984; print 'double R=%.12f (base %.12f)' to confirm the identity. (b) For J in {16, 32, 64}: free = arange(0, 2*J) on h2, run _lbfgs_block(h2, free, maxiter=200, deadline=slice) with beta=0, then a second pass with beta=1e4 (120 it); print 'toe J=%d R=%.9f dR=%+.2e min=%.3e max=%.3e' including the min/max of the optimized toe cells relative to their staircase initial values. Keep the best by exact R_of. (c) If the best has R > R(base)+1e-9, spend the remaining time alternating, to deadline-0.7 s: _lbfgs_block on the *union* of the toe window and _peak_window(frac=0.05) shifted to the toe (i.e. arange(0, 4*J_best)), beta=0 and beta=1e4, with a rank-prune-free exact polish; accept only strict improvements. (d) Return the best array among the base (84992) and all 169984 candidates by exact R_of; if none beats the base by >1e-12, return the base unchanged and print 'toe refinement: no gain'.

The decisive read-out is the toe sweep: if dR grows monotonically with J and is > +1e-6 at J=64, the ramp really is toe-discretisation limited and T44 should continue at J=128/256; if dR <= 1e-8 for all J, the toe is not the bottleneck and T44 is exhausted — that closes the track's premise rather than its parameters.

plan.analysis: The record 0.941243 is saturated: ~84 documented failures on that construction, all local height moves, no gain in 20+ generations. I keep one main slot there but bet on a genuinely untried move class (creating a gap inside the tallest spikes and pumping that mass into them). The most promising real headroom is T37: its family is the truncated x^-p edge-singular shape, and the analytic fact f=x^-1/2 gives f*f exactly constant on the support (R≈0.903 for the pure two-sided profile), yet T37's parametrization clipped p<=0.5, used sub=8 rasterization and a cap, so it only reached 0.882. A capping-free exact cell-average rasterization at high N plus L-BFGS should jump that track. For the backtrack I pick the never-pushed 0.939644 basin p0217 and give it the high-beta 1e7 cycle plus the coarse re-polish that recently gained elsewhere.

experiments.hypothesis: The record's f*f ramp steepness at its support edges is set by the height of the outermost tallest cells. Every previous mass move (toe replacement F485/F533, rank-pruning F509, pedestal) either smoothed the outer cells or removed the *smallest* cells. Untried: keep the tall spike but cut a gap immediately around it and pump that gap mass into the spike itself, which sharpens the f*f corner at constant total mass without touching the far tails.

experiments.hypothesis: The T37 family is the capped x^-p edge-singular shape, but its parametrization clipped p<=0.5, added a plateau offset, and rasterized with only sub=8 steps, so it never represented the pure two-sided x^-1/2 cell averages. plan.analysis: The record 0.941243 has survived ~140 local probes: height moves, toe/edge profiles, prolongation, smoothing/warps, softmax, phase, rank pruning, gap+spike. The evidence says it is a saturated discrete local optimum; more local polish is wasted. I bet main on a global low-frequency multiplicative basin-hop that moves mass between regions. T45's p0626 is a different 56%-zero basin; it has never had zero revival, so revive right-tail zeros. Bold slot builds a spike-plus-plateau parametric family from Code Zero, a genuinely different construction from edge/height local search.

experiments.hypothesis: Local height, toe, smoothing and warp moves all fail because they do not move mass globally. A low-frequency multiplicative field plus block-constant factors changes the large-scale mass distribution while retaining the record's fine structure; short block-L-BFGS screens many such moves cheaply.
experiments.change: Use start=p0616 and keep its helpers. Loop until the deadline: draw M in {2,4,8,16}, sigma in {0.02,0.05,0.10}, phases phi_m uniform, coefficients a_m ~ N(0,sigma), and form h' = h * exp(sum_m a_m sin(2*pi*m*x + phi_m)); also try multiplying by a random block-constant lognormal field with B in {8,32,128}. Rescale each candidate. Evaluate exact R. For each candidate run _lbfgs_block on B=512 block-sum variables for about 0.25 s, keep the 6 best exact-R candidates, then run _polish on each with a 5-6 s cap. Accept only strict R > 0.941243. If any candidate gains, restart perturbations around the new best with sigma halved. Print pre-polish and post-polish R for every retained candidate. Deadline-guard all stages and keep going until close to the end.

Reviving a controlled fraction of those zeros with low-amplitude mass taken from the tallest cells can flatten the descending f*f tail, as far-tail revival did on other high-zero basins (F157/F183). plan.analysis: The record p0616 is a saturated discrete local optimum: ~90 moves on this construction have failed, including toe replacement, sub-cell splits, upsampling, multigrid, block models and multiplicative fields. What has not been tried is a surrogate that changes the denominator: the exact max makes the gradient a single-knot spike, so the top plateau cannot be flattened. Slot 1 bets on a robust top-q max. Slot 3 revives F291's coarse-to-fine ladder, which moves large-scale mass where L-BFGS is well-conditioned. Slot 2 fixes T46: its family optimisation was numerically broken (raw R printed as 9.6e12, np.convolve O(N^2), final N stuck at 8192), so the spike+plateau family has never really been measured; fixed it should reach ~0.86 and is the only route to a genuinely different basin.

experiments.hypothesis: The record's ||f*f||_inf is attained on a near-tie plateau (18% of knots within 0.1% of max). With the exact max the gradient is 1/Lmax at one knot, so L-BFGS cannot flatten the top region; a robust max (mean of the top-q fraction of knots) gives a gradient spread over the whole top and lets mass move from the tails into the plateau, which is exactly what raises R.

plan.analysis: The record is a saturated exact 2x staircase (p0391/F288): every fine cell equals its partner, so all height-space moves stay in a measure-zero symmetric subspace, and ~150 local moves have failed. The one direction never probed at fine resolution is pair asymmetry — the record's pair-sum gradient vanishes (p0351: local optimum at 42496), but the curvature in the pair-difference subspace is untested, and a negative direction there is exactly the escape. T47's coarsening ladder produced a coarse optimum (0.9383 prolonged) that does not lift, so vary the phase of aggregation rather than the ladder. T46's family is its own 0.83 basin; give it power-law spikes and seed it from the record's own coarse profile to see how far that family really reaches.

experiments.hypothesis: p0616 is an exact 2x staircase, so h[2i]==h[2i+1] for all i. Every move so far has stayed either in the pair-sum direction (block/additive/log rescale, all fail) or in unrestricted multiplicative noise (F550, fails). The pair-difference subspace h[2i]=a(1+e_i), h[2i+1]=a(1-e_i) is exactly mass-preserving per pair, keeps the 42496-resolution profile's pair sums fixed, and has never been sampled systematically. If the record has any negative curvature in that subspace, some smooth e will raise exact R immediately without any optimizer.
experiments.change: Copy p0616 helpers verbatim (_conv, _knots, R_of, _fun_grad, _lbfgs_log, _lbfgs_block, _rescale, _peak_window, _polish). Let M=N//2=42496, a=h[0::2]. Candidate rule: h2[0::2]=a*(1+e), h2[1::2]=a*(1-e), clip to >=0, _rescale, R_of. Build e as a smooth low-frequency field: e = sum_{k=1..6} c_k*sin(2*pi*f_k*i/M + ph_k) with f_k log-uniform in [1,64], c_k random normal, then normalize max|e|=1. For 100 random field draws and delta in {1e-4,1e-3,1e-2,3e-2} evaluate exact R (~400 R_of calls), print the best few. Also include 3 fixed structured probes: single-sinusoid e at f=1,2,4 and a linear ramp e_i=(2i/M-1). Take the top-3 candidates by R, run p0616's _polish on each (beta 0/1e3/1e4 + two peak windows, ~8 s each, shared deadline), plus _polish on the untouched record as fallback; return the best exact R. Use the whole budget; if all probes lose, spend the remainder on extra fields with larger delta.

experiments.hypothesis: p0642's downward ladder coarsened only by pairing (2,2,2,...), prolongated one final coarse solution and got 0.9383 at fine resolution — worse than the record. If the coarse problem's optimum were phase-invariant, this would be conclusive; but the pairing phase (offset 0 vs 1) and block size (2 vs 3) select genuinely different mass aggregations, and each prolonged candidate gets its own fine polish. The coarse level is a smoothing of the objective whose optimum direction may only be useful when lifted immediately from that level, not from the deepest level.
experiments.change: From p0642, keep its coarsening/prolongation helpers. Define C(h,k,o): aggregate k consecutive cells starting at offset o (pad the ragged tail by cumulative-mass interpolation), value = mean. plan.analysis: The 0.941243 staircase is saturated: ~150 mutations on it fail, including coarse ladders (F557), aggregation-phase sweeps (F563), pair-difference probes (F648), block descent (F564), toe rewriting (F533/F539) and all beta/p-norm surrogates. Its profile is a near-rectangular f*f (18% of knots within 0.1% of max, 43% within 5%, argmax 0.417) so R is limited by the plateau's residual tilt and the flank ramps, not by a missing spike. I bet one thing is left: a second-order (Gauss-Newton/Chebyshev) step that raises the whole near-max plateau at once under h>=0, which no first-order method performs. Elsewhere I bet on (a) T46's new capped power-law family, which is rising fast but whose last run collapsed the spike and never escalated past N=8192, and (b) p0032, an untouched 0.939463 basin that has never seen the modern beta ladder.

experiments.hypothesis: R's gradient is a single-max indicator, so L-BFGS can only tilt the plateau one knot at a time; a Gauss-Newton step on the whole near-max knot set (min ||J_A d - (M-L_A)||^2 + lam||d||^2, h+d>=0) raises all of them simultaneously and lifts R further than any first-order path.
experiments.change: Copy p0646's helpers. Add `knots(h)=np.concatenate(([0],fftconvolve(h,h),[0]))`. Define the GN step: L=knots(h), M=L.max(), A={j: L[j] >= (1-kappa)*M} with kappa=0.05 (then 0.02, 0.01 in later passes); residual r = M - L[A]; solve (J^T W J + lam*I)d = J^T W r with CG (40 iters) where Jd = 2*fftconvolve(d,h)[:N] scattered to A (full L-index length 2N-1) and J^T v = 2*correlate(v_full,h)[N-1:2N-1], W=1; lam from 1e-2*mean|J^T r| down by 10x each outer iteration. Outer loop 8-10 times: compute d, then backtrack alpha in {1,0.5,0.25,0.125,2}, take the first with h+alpha*d>=0 and R strictly better; print RMS residual of the plateau and R each iteration. Finish with p0646's `_polish` (beta 0,1e3,1e4 and peak windows 0.05/0.15) using all remaining time; return the best exact R seen (base as fallback).
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941250-0.941270 (stretch 0.94130). Diagnostic: the near-max RMS deviation from M must drop >2x while R rises; if the residual drops 5x with R flat, the plateau is not the binding constraint and the flank/tail structure is, closing that direction.

experiments.hypothesis: T46's 0.842268 came from the new capped one-sided power-law family at N=8192, but the run collapsed the spike (max/mean 1.98 instead of >20) and never escalated past 8192; one spike cannot fit the asymmetric record, so a second edge spike plus a properly budgeted 1024->65536 ladder should realise the family's real value.
experiments.change: From p0645, extend rasterize to two independently placed one-sided capped power laws, f = d + c*plat + A1*min(cap1,(dist(x,p1,side1)+eps1)^-p1) + A2*min(cap2,(dist(x,p2,side2)+eps2)^-p2) (14 params; same bounds, caps 10-1e4, subcells=8). Optimise at N=1024 with differential_evolution (popsize 12, maxiter 120, init containing p0645's params zero-padded plus 20 random) using exact R_of, keeping the top 2 sets. Then escalate 1024->4096->16384->65536 (and ->169984 if >10 s remain) by cumulative-mass prolongation, at each level running p0616's `_lbfgs_log` with beta in {0,1e3,1e4} (~3 s each) and `_peak_window` block polish (~2 s), keeping the best exact R at each level and carrying the top-2 tracks. Print per-level R, max/mean and the f*f argmax fraction; return the best exact R over all levels and _polish(p0645) as fallback.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.87-0.89 at N=65536 (vs track best 0.842268), stretch 0.91. Diagnostic: final max/mean must exceed 20 (last run: 1.98, i.e. the spike was annihilated) and f*f argmax must sit away from 0.5; if max/mean still collapses after escalation, grid escalation itself destroys the spike and the family must be fitted with the ramp+polish machinery only at the final grid.

experiments.hypothesis: p0032 (0.939463, gen 154, an alternative handed back early) is a distinct basin whose only child scored 0.8816, so it has never seen the modern pipeline (log-space exact-max L-BFGS, aggressive beta homotopy to 1e7, peak-window block polish, 2x prolongation); that pipeline added 1e-4..1e-3 to comparable 0.94 basins.

plan.analysis: The record p0646 is a saturated exact 2x staircase; local, coarse, edge, zero and staircase-splitting moves have all failed on it. I keep the main slot on the strongest line but change the attack: retry the killed Gauss-Newton plateau-flattening idea at half resolution (where the staircase is exactly represented), with a strictly capped FFT/CG budget so it cannot time out. T48 needs a structural move rather than another polish; p0653's early f*f maximum suggests mass should be transferred from its tallest early cells into a right-tail ramp. T45 gained by right-side zero revival; I extend that to a rank-prune plus two-sided revival on p0633, which is new on this construction.

experiments.hypothesis: p0654's Gauss-Newton step on the near-max knot set is the right way to flatten the f*f plateau, but it was killed by an inefficient full-resolution implementation. p0646 is an exact 2x staircase, so pairwise-mean coarsening to N=42496 represents the same continuous f with identical R at half the cost. A tightly budgeted FFT/CG Gauss-Newton there can equalise the near-max knots without timing out.
experiments.change: From p0646, first coarsen by pairwise mean (h[0::2]+h[1::2])/2 to N=42496; verify exact R matches the start within 1e-9. Then for kappa in {0.05,0.02,0.01}: L=_knots(h), M=L.max(), A={j: L[j] >= (1-kappa)M}; solve (J^T J + lambda I)d = J^T(M-L[A]) by at most 5 CG iterations, where J d is computed as 2*fftconvolve(h,d) on knots and J^T y as the existing _backprop with y padded to len(L). Use lambda=1e-8*trace-estimate, cap the whole GN stage at 12 s CPU, attempt h+d with clip>=0 and accept only if exact R rises via backtracking. Follow with p0646's _lbfgs_log(beta=0), beta ladder 1e3,1e4,1e5, and peak-window block polish, all deadline-guarded; return the best exact-R array and use the full 60 s.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941250-0.941270 (stretch 0.94130). Diagnostic: near-max RMS deviation from M should fall by >2x while R rises; if every GN step fails exact-R backtracking even at kappa=0.05, the record plateau is not locally flattenable in this subspace and the main line needs a different global construction.

experiments.hypothesis: p0653 (0.939463, N=169984, 15.3% zeros, f*f argmax at 0.159) has an early f*f maximum, so its right half likely carries too much mass while the left/peak region is over-tall. The modern beta ladder alone did not help, so instead directly transfer mass from the tallest early cells into a broad right-tail ramp, then reoptimise. This structural mass move has not been tried on T48.
experiments.change: From p0653: if N>100000, first try pairwise-mean coarsening by 2; accept the coarser array only if its exact R is within 1e-7 of the start (otherwise keep full N). For alpha in {0.005,0.010,0.020,0.040} times mean(h[h>0]), add to the right window [0.45N,N) a linear ramp weight w(i)=0.2+0.8*(i-lo)/(hi-lo) scaled by alpha, and remove exactly the added mass from the top 1% tallest cells proportionally to their excess over the 99th percentile. Rescale, compute exact R for all candidates, keep the top 3. Polish each with p0653's _lbfgs_log beta=0 for <=4 s, then beta in {1e3,1e4,1e5,1e6} for <=2 s each, then _lbfgs_block on the peak window and on the right-tail window. Iterate the best ramp once more around the winning alpha if time remains; return the best exact R and use the full budget.

plan.analysis: The record 0.941243 is saturated under cell-local L-BFGS and many smoothing/coarsening/rearrangement escapes. The most promising untested mechanism is a correct, efficient Gauss-Newton plateau-flattening step: prior attempts died on an IndexError and full-resolution cost, not on the idea. Slot 1 fixes that at the exact 2x-coarsened level with FFT matvecs. Slot 2 tries a genuinely different spectral flat-target construction from Code Zero. Slot 3 revives F390's low-dimensional continuous-edge block model on p0646, where global block moves might escape the cell-local optimum.

experiments.hypothesis: R's exact gradient sees only the single max knot, so L-BFGS cannot flatten the 18.24% near-max plateau. A corrected Gauss-Newton step on all knots within kappa of max can move many heights coherently and raise R.
experiments.change: From p0646, first coarsen by exact pairwise mean h2=(h[0::2]+h[1::2])/2 to N=42496 and verify R(h2) matches R(p0646) within 1e-9. Build knots L of length 2N+1, indices 0..2N; never index 2N+1. For kappa in {0.05,0.02,0.01}: A={j in 1..2N-1: L[j] >= (1-kappa)*max(L)}; r=L[A]-max(L). Solve (J_A^T J_A + lam I)d = J_A^T r by CG, where Jd = 2*conv(h,d)[A] and J^T y = 2*correlate(y_padded,h)[:N], using fftconvolve for N>1500. Cap CG at 40 iterations, lam in {1e-6,1e-4,1e-2}*||J^T r||. Backtracking line search over alpha in {1,0.5,0.25,...}: h_new=clip(h+alpha*d,0), accept if exact R(h_new)>R(h). After each GN step run 2 s of existing _polish. Repeat until deadline-3 s, keep best exact R. Also try the same GN at full N=84992 if time remains, with capped CG.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941250-0.941265. Diagnostic: near-max RMS deviation from max should fall by >2x while exact R rises. If R stays 0.941243 after all kappa/lam, the plateau is a true coordinated local optimum and GN cannot help.

experiments.hypothesis: R=1 iff f*f is flat. Instead of optimizing R directly, design a nearly flat target g on [0,2], take its Fourier square root with random antisymmetric phases, inverse-transform and rectify to get f. This searches a different space and may find a new flat-autoconvolution basin.
experiments.change: From Code Zero, set N=4096. Define a target g on 2N grid: g=1 on [0.10,1.90] with raised-cosine edges of width w in {0.02,0.05,0.10}, plus 8 low-frequency real Fourier ripple coefficients. Compute G=fft(g). Set F=sqrt(max(G,0))*exp(i*phi), where phi is antisymmetric with 16 free real phase coefficients (phi[0]=0, phi[-k]=-phi[k]). Form f=real(ifft(F)) on the first N samples, clip to >=0, rescale. Optimize (w, ripple coeffs, phase coeffs) ~25 params by differential evolution (pop 20, 30 gens) then Nelder-Mead, maximizing exact R at N=4096 with fftconvolve. Keep best; if R>0.8, prolongate to N=16384 by cumulative-mass interpolation and polish 10 s with log-L-BFGS and beta in {0,1e3,1e4}. Print best spectral R and the rectified fraction.
experiments.prediction: Aim >0.80, stretch 0.90. Diagnostic: if best spectral R is below 0.80, phase-designed flat targets cannot produce a competitive nonnegative compact f; if above 0.85, this is a new viable family worth continuing.

experiments.hypothesis: The record is an exact 2x staircase, so its heights are piecewise constant at scale 2. A low-dimensional continuous-edge block model can make global mass moves that cell-local L-BFGS cannot, and may find a better block configuration than the staircase.
experiments.change: Revive F390's continuous-edge constant-block model on p0646. Use K=48 blocks: cumulative softmax gap parameters e_1..e_{K-1}, log-heights a_1..a_K, plus a global log-scale. Rasterise exactly to N=8192 by cell-overlap averaging (each cell integral of piecewise-constant f over [0,1]). Seed the gaps from quantiles of p0646's cumulative mass (including its zero cells), and heights from block means. Objective exact R via fftconvolve. Run Powell bounded multi-restart (3 restarts, 8 s total), then free log-space L-BFGS 8 s. Prolongate the best block model to N=84992 by exact rasterisation and run p0646's _polish for 10 s. Also compare R of the best N=8192 block model against R of a 8192 cumulative-mass coarsening of p0646. Keep best exact R over start and all candidates.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941250, stretch 0.941300. Diagnostic: if the N=8192 block optimum beats the coarsened record but the prolonged N=84992 polish does not beat 0.941243, the block model lacks fine structure; if both beat, block-level global moves are a useful new direction.

plan.analysis: The record is saturated at N=84992 and every exact-gradient, plateau Gauss-Newton, coarsening, and low-dimensional block revive on this record has failed. The strongest remaining main-line bet is to expose a new degree of freedom: double the record to N=169984 by exact duplication, then optimize the even/odd sub-cell split, which the N=84992 exact-max gradient cannot see. T49's spectral flat-target search is under-budgeted (8 s) and low-resolution, so a full-budget N=16384 version is worth continuing. T50's block model crashed before producing a valid program; it should be retried with the shape bug fixed and initialized from the record rather than random. Both explorations are judged against their own tracks.

experiments.hypothesis: The 0.941243 record is an exact 2x staircase, so it is a critical point at N=84992 but not necessarily at N=169984. Duplicating each height exactly preserves f, then allowing the two half-cells inside each old cell to split unequally gives a new sub-cell degree of freedom that can flatten the broad f*f plateau without any global mass move.
experiments.change: From p0665, build h2 of length 169984 by np.repeat(h,2). Run p0665's _lbfgs_log(h2, maxiter 200, beta=0), then beta=1e3 and beta=1e4, keeping exact R at N=169984. After each pass also run _lbfgs_block on the fine array around the f*f argmax with frac=0.05, then another global log pass. Use the remaining time alternating fine global and peak-window L-BFGS until deadline-3 s. Return the fine array if its exact R exceeds the base; otherwise return the base. Print fine R and the R of the pairwise-mean coarsened array.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941248-0.941262. Diagnostic: if fine R rises while the pairwise-mean coarsened R stays near 0.941243, sub-cell splitting is the mechanism; if fine R never exceeds 0.941243, the staircase is already optimal at half-cell scale.

experiments.hypothesis: p0664's spectral flat-target family reached 0.786748 in only 8 s at N=4096 with a small DE. Its own result has only 0.68% of f*f knots near max, so it is far from saturated. A larger N, more ripple and phase parameters, and full-budget DE+NM+L-BFGS polish should reveal whether this family can become competitive.
experiments.change: From p0664, keep its spectral parameterization but set N=16384, n_rip=12, n_phase=24. Expand bounds to w in [0.02,0.20], ripples in [-0.5,0.5], phases in [-pi,pi]. Run differential evolution with pop 32 for 60 generations, then Nelder-Mead for up to 3000 evaluations. Prolongate the best spectral f to N=65536 by cumulative-mass interpolation, then run log-height L-BFGS with analytic gradient and beta in {0,1e3,1e4}, followed by a peak-window block polish, using all remaining time. Return the best valid construction found.

plan.analysis: The record basin is saturated: ~30 generations of local, coarse-ladder, block-model, upsample and sub-cell moves all returned the 0.941243 construction unchanged, and F585/F353 explain why — the exact 2x staircase (and its 2x prolongation) is a critical point, so every gradient-based escape sees zero first-order slope. Two untried levers remain: (a) escape through second-order information (a negative-curvature 'valley' direction in a reduced subspace, reached where the gradient vanishes), and (b) prevent the fine polish from collapsing back by constraining the step radius (a trust-region continuation from a coarse block model). I put the curvature probe on the main line because it is the one mechanism that acts precisely where all gradient escapes failed, and give the exploration slots the trust-region block continuation on T50 and a needle/zero-revival push on the distinct 0.939463 basin p0661.

experiments.hypothesis: p0670 (N=169984, R=0.941243) is a critical point of exact R, so every gradient-based escape (F288/F353/F585) is blind there; but the Hessian in a smooth 64-dim block-scaling subspace is computable cheaply from finite differences of the analytic gradient, and following its most negative / most nearly-flat eigen-direction over a deliberately large step (a valley crossing) can leave the local max, which no first-order move could do.
experiments.change: From p0670: h0 = rescaled base (N=169984). Build a reduced basis V of p=64 directions: v_i = Gaussian-smoothed indicator of block i of 64 consecutive cells (sigma = 1.5 block widths), each normalized to max|v_i|=1. Using the module's analytic R-gradient (project out the overall scaling direction), compute the projected gradient G_i = v_i . grad at h0 and the reduced Hessian H_ij by central differences of G_i along v_j (eps = 1e-5 * max(h0)), 2*p gradient evaluations (~15 s). Symmetrize H, eigendecompose, and take the ordering by eigenvalue (most negative first, then smallest |lambda|). For each of the top 4 directions d: w = sum_i d_i v_i, normalize ||w||_inf = 1; for t in the geometric ladder {+-1e-3, +-1e-2, +-3e-2, +-1e-1, +-3e-1, +-1.0} form h = clip(h0 * exp(t*w), 0, None), rescale, record exact R, and for the 4 best t run a short _lbfgs_log(maxiter 60) polish; keep the best. Then, with the remaining time, run 6 rounds of: pick a random combination of the 4 eigen-directions with random t in the same ladder, short polish, keep best; finish with a 3 s sharp _lbfgs_log plus a peak-window polish. Always return max(exact R) over {start, all candidates}; print the reduced Hessian's 5 smallest eigenvalues, the R along each t for the best direction, and the final exact R.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941250-0.941270. Diagnostic: the printed reduced Hessian eigenvalues reveal whether the record is a strict local max (all lambda <= 0) or already has a negative-curvature flat direction; if no t on the best eigen-direction exceeds 0.941243 even after polish, the basin is second-order closed in the smooth-scale subspace and the next probe must use a finer basis.

experiments.hypothesis: T50's block model was never really tested: p0672 rasterised the K=32 fit and then handed it to an unconstrained full-resolution polish, which slides straight back to the record, so the experiment measured the polish, not the block model. If the coarse block optimum genuinely carries a better large-scale mass distribution, a trust-region polish that refuses big per-cell moves (radius shrunk gradually) will keep some of that gain instead of erasing it.
experiments.change: From p0672: (1) refit the K=32 continuous-edge block model (softmax gaps + log heights, exact rasterization matrix) with Powell from 6 restarts (record mass quantiles, equal-mass quantiles, random perturbations), and ALSO K=16 and K=64; print for each the *pure* block-model R at its own resolution and the exact R after rasterizing to N=84992. (2) Take the best rasterization h_r (N=84992); then run a trust-region continuation: u0 = log(h_r + tiny); for rho in {0.7, 0.35, 0.18, 0.09, 0.045, 0.02, 0.01}, run _lbfgs_log with box bounds [u0-rho, u0+rho] on the log-heights (implement a bounded log-L-BFGS variant; ~2 s each), recording exact R after each level, and use the level's result as the warm start of the next but keep the bound centred on that level's own start (do NOT recentre on h_r). (3) Keep the best exact R over {base, all block rasterizations, all trust-region levels}; spend the remaining time with sharp _lbfgs_log plus peak-window polish on the best. Return the best array (never worse than base).
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941250; a useful secondary signal is whether the K=32 rasterized R at N=84992 already exceeds 0.941243 before polishing, and whether the rho-ladder R decreases monotonically as rho shrinks. If every rho level ends at or below the base and the pure block R is no better than the record coarsened to K blocks, large-scale block moves on this construction are genuinely dead and T50 should be retired.

experiments.hypothesis: p0661 is a structurally different basin (0.939463, N=169984, 15.3% zeros, f*f argmax at 0.159 rather than the record's ~0.4), so it is not merely a worse copy of the record and its dominant-cell heights have never been searched directly. The exact-R gradient is near-useless when the argmax knot switches between near-tied knots, so a direct coordinate/needle search over the few tallest cells, plus controlled zero-revival in the dead runs (which paid off on p0204/p0229 and on F551's 56%-zero basin), should move this construction where gradient methods stall.
experiments.change: From p0661: rescale, then Stage A — needle search: take the 16 largest heights; for each of the top 8, try multiplicative factors {0.55,0.7,0.85,1.15,1.35,1.8} (rescale, exact R each, cheap), and also joint factors on the top-4 and top-16 sets; accept any strict improvement and re-polish the accepted candidate with a 2 s _lbfgs_log. Stage B — controlled zero-revival: find maximal runs of exact zeros; for each run longer than 8 cells, fill a fraction q in {0.25,0.5,1.0} of the run (from the left end, the right end, and both) with the mean of the adjacent non-zero heights, rescale, short polish, keep if exact R improves. Stage C — deadline loop: alternate a beta ladder {1e3,1e4,1e5,1e6,1e7} (global _lbfgs_log, ~3 s each) with peak-window block polishes whose window fraction cycles over {0.02,0.05,0.1,0.2} and a 2x mass-preserving prolongation-to-339968 polish if time allows; always keep max exact R and return the best, printing the R after each stage and the final zeros fraction.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.9400-0.9412 from 0.939463. Diagnostic: a gain from Stage A means the loss there is a single dominant cell's height; a gain from Stage B means the dead runs are suppressing a ramp; if both are silent and Stage C only reproduces 0.939463, this basin is saturated at a distinctly lower level and the record's shape is genuinely privileged.

plan.analysis: The 0.941243 record has resisted ~170 local, multi-resolution, block-model, warp, split, Hessian and needle attacks: it is a critical point at both N=42496 and N=169984, and every transfer from weaker basins caps at ~0.88-0.90, so from-scratch families cannot reach it. Two facts remain unexploited: (i) coarsening the exact staircase preserves R exactly, so a *very* coarse (N~1300) re-optimisation has never been tried — all coarsening so far stopped at N=42496 with standard polish; (ii) the record's f*f plateau is 6% above its flat width, so any real flattening is worth ~1e-3. The T51 basin (0.939463) has had height needles and zero revival but never support-length (cropping) moves. L9 is the one line still gaining fast (+0.010 in its last cycle), so its cycle/ladder recipe should be continued.

experiments.hypothesis: The record is a critical point at every resolution tried (42496, 84992, 169984) because all coarsening stopped at 2x, where the coarse problem is still the same fine basin. Coarsening by 128x (mass-preserving pairwise mean, which preserves R exactly on the staircase) gives an N=1328 problem whose landscape is genuinely different: from there, multi-start log-L-BFGS plus perturbations can restructure the global skeleton, and prolongating back with polish at each level can land on a better fine critical point.
experiments.change: From p0670 (N=169984): (1) rescale, then coarsen by pairwise mean 7 times to N=1328 (exact, R preserved). (2) At N=1328 run 12 restarts: the coarsened record plus 11 copies with log-normal multiplicative noise (sigma 0.1-0.5 applied to cells above the mean), each optimised with the module's log-space L-BFGS (beta ladder 0, 1e2, 1e3, 300 iters total each, cheap at N=1328), keep the 3 best distinct candidates by exact R. (3) Prolongate each 2x step by step (1328->2656->...->169984) with mass-preserving pairwise duplication, then at each level: sharp beta=0 log-L-BFGS (30-60 iters) + one peak-window block polish (window frac 0.05-0.2); at levels <= 10624 add 6 perturbed restarts (sigma 0.05-0.2) and keep the best. (4) Keep the overall best exact R at the finest level reached; use all remaining time on alternating sharp global and peak-window polishes at that level. Print coarse-best R and R at every level.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.94130-0.9420. Diagnostic: the printed coarse-level R after stage (2) — if it exceeds the record's coarse R (0.941243 exactly, since the staircase coarsens losslessly) the structure really was suboptimal at scale; if no restart beats 0.941243 at N=1328, the record is scale-invariantly locally optimal and this whole escape family is closed.

experiments.hypothesis: T51's basin (0.939463, f*f argmax at 0.159, only 9.8% of knots near max) is dominated by an early peak with a long declining flank, i.e. too much mass sitting at the far end inflates ||f*f||_inf. Height needles (F593), tail-ramp mass transfer (F575) and zero revival all failed, but support-length has never been searched: truncating the profile changes the shape, not just the scale, so cropping the harmful end can lower the max while barely touching the L2 mass.
experiments.change: From p0681 (N=84992): (1) cropping sweep — for each end separately (left, right, and both), for crop fractions f in {0.002,0.005,0.01,0.02,0.04,0.07,0.10,0.15,0.20,0.30,0.40} of N, truncate that many cells (drop them, do not zero-pad), rescale, compute exact R; print the full R-vs-f curve for each end. (2) Take the best 3 cropping candidates, re-optimise the 32 cells adjacent to each new edge with a 2 s block L-BFGS, then a 2 s global log L-BFGS; keep only strict improvements over 0.9394633. (3) Deadline loop on the best: alternate sharp global log L-BFGS (3 s) with peak-window block polishes (window frac cycling 0.02/0.05/0.1) and a beta ladder {1e3,1e4,1e5} pass; always keep max exact R and return it with a final printout of zeros fraction and argmax position.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.9396-0.9410 from 0.939463. Diagnostic: a crop curve peaking at a nonzero fraction means the far tail is harmful (and quantifies how much); a monotonically decreasing curve means the support is already right and this basin's loss is purely geometric, closing support-length as a lever here.

experiments.hypothesis: L9 is the only line still gaining fast: p0662 took +0.0102 in its single second cycle (0.8725 -> 0.8827) using beta-homotopy cycles at fixed N, and its f*f has only 2.1% of knots within 0.1% of max, so it is far from the flat-profile limit and the same recipe with more cycles plus one more resolution level should keep paying.
experiments.change: From p0662 (N=32768): (1) run 6 more full cycles at N=32768 (a cycle = beta-homotopy ladder {1e3,1e4,1e5,1e6,1e7} global log L-BFGS, ~2.5 s each, then peak-window block polish with window frac cycling 0.02/0.05/0.1/0.2), printing R after every cycle and keeping the best. (2) If two consecutive cycles fail to improve by >1e-6, prolongate mass-preservingly by 2x to N=65536 (cumulative-mass linear interpolation), rescale, and continue the same cycle loop plus one sharp beta=0 global polish at the start of each cycle. (3) Spend the last 5 s on a sharp full-vector L-BFGS at the largest N reached. Return the best exact-R array.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.895-0.915. plan.analysis: The record has survived ~170 probes on its own construction: every smooth gradient, polish, block-model, coarsening and prolongation move returns it unchanged, and it is an exact 4x staircase, so its effective shape is 42496 cells. I bet on three things. (a) One genuinely new objective on the record: a capped-sum 'flooding' surrogate that explicitly rewards the 57% of f*f knots sitting below ~1.05*max and lets the peak drop — evaluated at the gauge-equivalent 42496 grid so iterations are 4x cheaper. (b) L9, the only line compounding gains (2.5e-3, 2.3e-3, 1.9e-3 per cycle) and it never reached its own prolongation step; force N=65536 with a beta ladder rescaled for the finer spacing. (c) A different function space from Code Zero: free-breakpoint non-uniform step functions, exact O(K^2) knot-sum R, finite-difference L-BFGS — the only cheap way to buy sub-cell resolution at the sharp f*f ramps that cause the flatness deficit.

experiments.hypothesis: R's exact gradient cannot flatten the record's top: the max knot absorbs all the peak-side signal while the many knots 5-30% below max contribute only through ||g||_2^2, and at this construction that gradient is saturated. A capped-sum surrogate min(g, (1-delta)*max(g)) is concave in g: it puts unit gradient on every knot below the cap and zero on the peak, so the descent direction must trade peak height for shoulder height, i.e. perform exactly the mass transfer that has been stalled. Working at N=42496 (exact 4x pairwise-mean coarsening of the record, R preserved to machine precision) gives 4x cheaper iterations and breaks the 'fine-grid critical point' argument, since the coarse problem is not the same optimisation.
